scalesUsed.notes: G - A - B - C - D - E - F# - G
scalesUsed.application: Provides the diatonic chord foundation (Em, C, D, G) connecting the minor verse to the major resolution
Shapes the iconic acoustic intro riff and bluesy fills around the Em7 chord

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian / Ionian duality with rugged, melancholic folk-rock resonance
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: E minor is the relative minor of G major

mainProgression.description: The classic minor-to-major narrative progression. Starting on the introspective Em (vi) and rising through subdominant C (IV) and dominant D (V) into a warm tonic G (I) resolution.

sectionProgressions.description: Iconic acoustic riff built on Em7 and D with rhythmic percussive mutes and single-note bass walkups
Storytelling progression moving from minor introspection to major warmth and back
The memorable sing-along hook balancing minor depth with open G major resolution
Open position E minor / G major scale study highlighting hammer-ons and chord-tone embellishments

harmonicFunction: Em (vi) - Relative minor establishing the searching, contemplative atmosphere
C (IV) - Subdominant chord adding hope and emotional lift
D (V) - Dominant chord creating natural harmonic resolution pulling toward G
G (I) - Tonic chord representing the elusive, radiant 'heart of gold'

techniques.name: Acoustic Hammer-On Embellishments
techniques.description: Hammering open strings into chord tones (such as hammering the 2nd fret on the D and A strings) to create Neil Young's organic acoustic signature sound

notes: Hammer open D string to 2nd fret (E note) on beat 1
Quick transition to D major with open high E string ringing
Return cleanly to Em with a strong downward acoustic strum
sequence: Fret the low E and open strings for Em
Hammer index/middle finger onto the 2nd fret of the D string while striking
Quickly shift to the open D chord shape on beat 3
Snap back into full Em with a percussive right-hand brush
tips: Strike with the fingertip directly behind the fret wire for a crisp hammer-on snap
Let the open strings continue ringing while hammering for maximum acoustic resonance
Keep right wrist relaxed and bouncing at 88 BPM

techniques.name: Walking Basslines & Single-Note Pickups
techniques.description: Playing single bass notes (such as open E to 2nd fret F# to 3rd fret G) between chord changes to propel the rhythm forward

notes: Low E string: open E (0) to 2nd fret F# (2) to 3rd fret G (3)
5th string: open A (0) to 2nd fret B (2) to 3rd fret C (3)
Seamlessly blend single picked notes into full downward chord strums
sequence: End the chord bar with a single bass pickup on beat 4-and
Land squarely on the root note of the next chord on beat 1
Brush through the treble strings on beat 2
Repeat the walking sequence to connect each section
tips: Keep the volume of the single notes equal to the full strums
Use a firm, confident pick attack on the low bass strings
Do not rush the transition — maintain the leisurely 88 BPM country-rock pulse

sections.name: Intro Riff
sections.description: Neil Young starts alone on his Martin dreadnought, strumming the iconic Em7 - D - Em motif with sharp rhythmic accents and hammer-ons.
notes: Hit the low E bass string firmly on beat 1
Execute the clean snap onto the Em7 chord
Switch smoothly into D major, then strike back into Em
Let the open strings ring with authentic Harvest-era acoustic tone
sections.exerciseLabel: Neil Young Iconic Em7-D-Em Harvest Riff

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: The lyrical verse cycles through Em, C, D, and G, blending open chord strums with single bass note transitions.
notes: Warm, relaxed strumming on the Em chord
Transition to C on the 5th string (3rd fret)
D major creates dominant tension before resolving into full open G
Walking bass line on string 6 leads back into Em

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The chorus elevates the vocal theme with ringing open chords: Em to G, then resolving to C and back to G.
notes: Increase strumming intensity for the vocal hook
Let the open high E and B strings ring out continuously
Seamlessly pivot between Em and G shapes

sections.name: Scale Practice Exercise
sections.description: Open position E minor pentatonic scale run connecting the core notes used in Neil Young's acoustic fills and riffs.
notes: Practice alternate picking through the open strings
Focus on accurate finger placement on 2nd and 3rd frets
Incorporate subtle vibrato when landing on the low and high E notes
sections.exerciseLabel: Open E Minor Pentatonic Acoustic Run

guitar.recommended: Martin D-28 or D-45 Dreadnought Acoustic
guitar.pickup: Natural acoustic microphone capture (Neumann KM84 or Shure SM81 style)

amp.recommended: Acoustic amplifier or direct to studio console with analog preamp

effects.other: Harmonica in the key of G on a neck rack (optional for authentic Neil Young performance)

beginner.title: Master the 4 Fundamental Chords (Em, C, D, G)
steps: Learn open Em, C, D, and G chord shapes
Practice the verse progression (Em - C - D - G) with steady quarter-note strums
Work on smooth finger placement without muting adjacent open strings
Play along with the recording at 70 BPM to build confidence

intermediate.title: Nail the Signature Intro Riff & Hammer-Ons
steps: Master the Em7 chord shape (0-2-2-0-3-0 or 0-2-0-0-3-0) with the pinky/ring finger on the B string
Practice the snap hammer-on from open D string to 2nd fret
Incorporate the walking bass notes (0-2-3 on the low E string)
Bring the complete song up to the authentic 88 BPM recording tempo

advanced.title: Expressive Dynamics & Harmonica Accompaniment
steps: Replicate Neil Young's loose, emotive right-hand strumming dynamics
Add subtle syncopated upstroke accents on offbeats
Mount a G harmonica on a neck rack and practice simultaneous acoustic rhythm and harmonica leads
Perform the entire song with compelling storytelling presence

commonMistakes: Playing too stiffly — Neil Young's rhythm is loose, expressive, and human
Muting the open high E string when fretting the D chord
Rushing the tempo beyond 88 BPM; the song breathes at a laid-back pace
Over-complicating the hammer-ons instead of keeping them snappy and percussive
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Em, C, D, G open chord finger warm-up
5 minutes: Intro riff hammer-on mechanics (Em7 - D - Em) with a metronome at 80 BPM
5 minutes: Walking bass line pickups connecting verse chords
5 minutes: Chorus flow (Em - G - C - G) with dynamic strumming accents
5 minutes: Full run-through from intro to outro
focusAreas: Crisp hammer-on articulation on the D string
Accurate bass string targeting on beats 1 and 3
Loose, rhythmic wrist action at 88 BPM
Capturing the rugged Harvest acoustic tone
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 75 BPM to lock in the Em7 - D intro riff timing
Advance to 88 BPM once the hammer-ons and chord changes are seamless
Practice feeling the pulse on beats 2 and 4 to develop organic groove
Ensure steady tempo during the transition between verse and chorus
